And because a single river flowed forth from that earring of gold, Mahādeva named it Svarṇodakā; and because a second [river] flowed from the auspicious crown made of Jāmbūnada gold, [he named it likewise]. || 8.22.30 ||
A holy river began to flow, and they called it Jāmbūnadī.
This place named Pañcanada is situated near Japyeśvara;
the great-souled Jaṭodā has explained the fruit of these [five rivers].
And that divine Pañcanada and that god Japyeśvara—
Having fasted for three nights, gone there, bathed, and worshipped the wielder of the trident, || 3.3 ||
Having gratified the Brāhmaṇas, a man who dies anywhere whatsoever shall become an attendant of Nandīśvara and have his abode in the Ocean of Milk.
But he who gives up his life-breaths—so difficult to relinquish—at Japyeshvara, whether by means of a formal vow or otherwise, shall become a Gaṇapati unto me. ||35||
Ever equal to Nandīśvara, he is indeed eternal, imperishable, and undecaying;
he is my beloved attendant by my side and is highly esteemed.
"Any man who comes to Japyeśvara and Pañcanada and casts off his body there,
he shall always be my most excellent Gaṇapa, equal to Tvaṣṭṛ and possessing a beautiful form forever.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter in the Skanda Purāṇa.
Sanatkumāra said:
The Blessed One, the Lord of the gods of gods, Hara, the master of all beings,
spoke to the Goddess Umā, the daughter of the mountain king, O Master of Speech.
"O Goddess, I shall consecrate the god Nandīśvara, the lord of beings; I shall summon the Gaṇas. Or what do you think, O Auspicious One? ||2||
The Goddess said:
"O Lord of Gods, my eldest son Nandin deserves all this— the sovereignty over the seven worlds as well as that of the lords of the Gaṇas."
Sanatkumāra said:
Then that Blessed Lord, the destroyer of the enemies of the gods,
facing the east, performed the invocation of the lords of the Gaṇas at that time.
Then, O great sage, thousands of leaders of the Gaṇas, filled with joy, arrived there at that very moment—
all those lords of all the worlds who are Rudras dwelling in heaven.
O Vyāsa, there are other Rudras, the best of their kind, whose number is not known;
and those who are the protectors of the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa), O Sage, such as Ahirbudhnya and others,
as well as the Kapālins, Aṃśis, Viśokas, the hundred-eyed, and the hundred-faced.
The Anantarudras and others who have a hundred faces and a hundred bellies,
whose hands and feet are everywhere, who are stationed in all directions,
endowed with the powers such as *aṇimā*, and who are the causes of the manifestation of Brahmā.
All the lords of the worlds have arrived; listen to them, O great sage! ||9||
Then [he appeared] with a formidable face, his countenance adorned with a frown;
white as a conch shell, a pearl necklace, or water; possessing tusks, wearing garlands, and having three eyes;
with a thousand matted locks rising in a crest, hair like flames, and large jaws.
He has fire and glowing embers for eyes, and his girdle is bound with serpents.
He had lightning for a tongue, a massive body, and likewise his penis was turned upward;
he wore a serpent as a sacred thread and likewise carried a battle-axe. || 12 ||
Wearing a girdle of muñja grass bound with serpents and bracelets made of snakes themselves,
and uttering roars resembling the crash of thunderbolts,
the leader of the hosts known as Diṇḍi was seen.
Surrounded by ten crores of beings equal to himself—
leaders of the Gaṇas, lords of the gods, and yogins of blazing splendor—
thereafter appeared Mahākeśa, who possessed a massive body and an erect penis.
Resembling three eyes and a hundred fires, roaring like the fall of a thunderbolt,
he danced and sang, performing various dances many times over;
with flaming fangs, a great laugh, broad shoulders, and bearing the Pināka bow.
Together with ten billion twice as many high-souled ones,
hosts of diverse forms appeared simultaneously;
they had the faces of lions, elephants, tigers, leopards, and panthers.
O Vyāsa, the leader of the Gaṇas named Soṣāḍhi arrived there.
Sanatkumāra said:
Then another arrived, O Vyāsa, possessing a radiance like the sun at the end of a Yuga.
His arms were a hundred yojanas long; he was naked and had an upward-pointing penis. His sexual organ was exceedingly large, his eyebrows hung down, and his nose was thick.
His face was round with large eyes, and his countenance was furrowed by a frown.
Extending five yojanas in width and likewise in length,
he bore four fangs in his mouth, white as a conch shell or the moon.
With five fires [around him], ears turned upward, noose in hand, and swift as thought,
he was seen surrounded by a hundred crores of his own likeness;
known as Bhārabhūti, he was endowed with the power of great yoga.
The leader of the Gaṇas approached the presence of the God of gods.

Then [he beheld Him] who has the luster of a Kunda flower, the moon, or a conch shell; who resembles a mass of snow or water; who possesses the brilliance of a lotus stalk or crystal; and who wears a girdle of ashes.
And he seized Aśanīhāsa, who was three-legged, clothed in rags,
hundred-bellied, three-headed, three-eyed, with hair standing erect on his head,
possessing fierce flaming locks, and wearing a tiger-skin as a garment.
Possessing the speed of the wind, with a great laugh, and having a girdle bound by serpents. || 26 ||
Mahoragakṛtāpīḍa, Śaṅku, Urdhvamehana, Bhasmapraharaṇa, Mahādaṃṣṭra, Mahāhanu,
Mahāgaṇapati, Vīra, and the one renowned as Jvara— [these are the lords].
And he beheld that leader of the hosts surrounded by a hundred crores [of followers].
Then another appeared, of gentle form, his limbs smeared with ashes,
bearing a trident in his hand, clad in the directions as his garment, and endowed with the power of great yoga.
Wearing many disguises and devoted to the yoga of meditation,
the lord known as Somavarṇa arrived, surrounded by hundreds of millions,
having been summoned by the God and coming as a leader of such hosts.
His body was covered with the ashes of a thousand flames; he possessed great eyes and a penis directed upwards.
Then another appeared, massive in body, spear-handed, and of great strength;
resembling the fire at the end of an eon, steadfast, and possessing the power of enduring fame.
He had the moon upon his crest, long hair, four arms, and was deep red in hue.
With one leg, massive bodies, three eyes, and tridents in their hands.
Surrounded by a hundred crores [of followers], Sthāṇu was present there;
that Rudra, the destroyer of all Asuras, was accompanied by his great attendants.
After him was Paṭṭasena, pure, with short feet and belly,
possessing a thousand arms and feet, a thousand eyes, and great majesty.
He has formidable fangs, wears black serpents as his garments,
possesses three eyes, bears the moon as a crest-ornament, and is adorned with a garland around his neck.
Known as Ugrasena, surrounded by a hundred crores,
he too came into the presence of the Lord, having been summoned by the Lord himself. Then another announced to the God, who bears the crescent moon:
The Lord has four faces, great splendor, and twenty-four eyes. || 38 ||
He has a thousand arms, a flaming mouth, great eyes, and an upward-pointing penis; he has formidable teeth, spike-like ears, and large claws.
Asipāṇi, Mahātejas, Śatapāda, Śatodara, Vidyutkeśa, Atihāsa, and likewise Ubhayatogati—
known as Ajaikapād— he was surrounded by hundreds of crores of them.
Abounding with golden stones and trees, it was like a mountain shrouded in clouds. ||41||
Sanatkumāra said:
Then another Gaṇapa, O Vyāsa, of great strength arrived;
he was wise, with faces on all sides, and possessed hands and feet on every side.
With short arms, thighs, and feet, he held a beautiful thunderbolt and was surrounded by eight hundred million beings equal to himself.
Then there came one renowned as Nikumbha, who had a hundred feet, bellies, and faces; and another of great strength named Vidyutkeśa,
who wore a garland of moons, was terrible, and moved about while laughing.
He holds a staff, has a large face, and possesses a radiance like that of a conch shell, a kunda flower, or the moon. ||45||
Surrounded by hundreds of millions of attendants, that supreme scorcher of enemies arrived;
then another, a lord of hosts surrounded by a thousand million,
wearing a garland of suns, arrived, performing great austerities.
He named Sūryāpyāyana is the supreme favorite of the god;
he is renowned for his great splendor, with bow in hand and possessing immense majesty.
Likewise, there is another named Sarpamāla, as well as Cakrābharaṇa. ||47-48||
Armed with a discus and possessing great splendor, with short feet and a protruding hip,
he is renowned in the world by the name Grahopāyana.
Surrounded by six hundred million attendants, he pursued him;
the mighty Śaṅkukarṇa also advanced with ten million attendants,
as did Nandika with ten and Piṅgākṣa with eight.
The Vināyaka known by the name Kuṣmāṇḍa is renowned as having sixty-four [attendants]. ||51||
Hiraṇyavarṇa with six, and likewise Ekapāda;
Dhūmrakeśa with twelve, and likewise Patākī with ten. (52)
Sahasraghaṇṭa with eighteen, Tapas with five, Sahasraśīrṣa with six, and Bhava surrounded by ten million. (53)
Vara approached with ten, Kumbhakarṇa likewise with eight;
Viṣvaksena with a thousand, and Anada indeed with a hundred.
Āveśana is surrounded by eight, and Pravartana by seven;
Mahārava is surrounded by a thousand hosts, O Lord of Gaṇas.
Caturmukha is surrounded by twelve, as is Bāhuprahāraka.
Mahākāla with a hundred [attendants], and likewise the Gaṇa Agniśikhara. ||56||
Ādityamūrdhā with ten million, and likewise Dhanāvaha;
Sannābha with one hundred, and Kukkuṭa with eight;
Kunda with fifteen, and another, Saṃkoṭaka.
Amoghabhūti with ten million followers, and likewise Aghabhūtika. || 58 ||
Ekapāda is the next with sixty [verses], and likewise Āraṇa with seven; Mahābala has nine, and Apasmāra is well-known [with eight]. (59)
Nīla, the lord of the gods, as well as Pūrṇabhadra and Nirṛti,
approached together with seventy crores [of followers].
They were surrounded by twenty hundred thousand times ten million crores.
And there, calamities arrived, accompanied by those endowed with the power of great yoga:
Bhūtas by the thousands of crores, Pramathas by three crores,
Vīrabhadra with sixty-four [crores], and the exceedingly powerful Vṛṣabha.
Megha, surrounded by ninety followers including Saudāminīmāla, arrived;
as did Prabhākara with twenty, Viṭpati, and the mighty Mahābala.
Girika, Meghanāda, Udara, and Maṇi also came.
Kāṣṭhakarṇa, the divine-souled Viśvarūpa, and the renowned [Viśvāmitra];
likewise Śatamanyu, the powerful Pañcākṣa, Tālaketu, Ṣaṇḍa, Kapālī, and Gajanāśana. || 64–65 ||
Saṃvartaka, as well as Caitra, the burner of the three worlds,
Lokāntaka, Dīptātman, and Hemakuṇḍala.
Mṛtyu, Yama, Kāla, and likewise Viṣahara; Śatamāya, Mahāmāya, and Sarvatrāśaraṇa as well. ||67||
Ekaśṛṅga is renowned, as is Bhṛṅgiriṭi;
these and other leaders of the Gaṇas who are secret and possess great strength.
There they all arrived, filled with joy, those mighty warriors skilled in various weapons; some singing, some running, and some dancing,
while others likewise played upon musical instruments and cymbals.
They went forth on chariots, elephants, and horses, while others rode upon monkeys.

Some were mounted upon celestial chariots, while others were among human beings; they were accompanied by tigers, lions, cats, serpents, and birds, as well as by many various beasts of prey, both small and diverse, and auspicious ones. || 71 ||
Some traveled by means of the Puṣpaka chariot or by intoxicated elephants; others, having set their hearts on it, went with Kinnaras, Uragas, and Cāraṇas,
or by means of vehicles equipped with excellent weapons or yoked with swans.
Others there, by the millions, mounted upon various celestial chariots;
and with kettledrums, conchs, clay drums, cymbals, small drums, horns, and gomukhas,
as well as with various musical instruments, paṭahas, and ekapuṣkaras, [they played].
With the resounding blasts of kettledrums and cymbals, and the booming sounds of āḍambara and ḍiṇḍima drums.
With frogs, flutes, lutes, and even with *tuṇava* drums;
with *dardara* drums, cymbals, and *kacchapa* drums, as well as with *paṇava* drums. ||76||
As great yogas were being played upon musical instruments, the Grandfather, the lotus-born Brahmā, arrived at the assembly of the gods,
surrounded on all sides by sages perfected in yoga, amidst a divine array of swans.
On the southern side is the Ṛgveda, adorned with divine earrings;
on the western side is the auspicious Sāmaveda, assuming various forms;
and on the northern side is the lord Atharvaveda, bearing fire in his eye. || 78–79 ||
The Yajurveda likewise stands to the east, assuming the form of lightning;
and the Itihāsas and Purāṇas stand as well, assuming various forms.
By means of a vehicle that shone before them, they too proceeded there;
the great yogi Janārdana, a devotee of Śiva, arrived there seated upon Garuḍa,
surrounded by all his own attendants.
Surrounded by auspicious, divine beings equal to himself who bore the forms of Viṣṇu,
Mahādeva, seeing that Nārāyaṇa had arrived,
spoke these words with a deep voice to Śambhu, the creator of the worlds. || 82-83 ||
"Listen to my words, O Viṣṇu; I shall speak them to you, Janārdana.
Grant the consecration to my most beloved daughter Nandinī.
Laughing, the Lord Nārāyaṇa spoke again to Śaṅkara.
“As you say, O Lord of Gods, so shall I do, O Bull-bannered One!
You are the God even of the gods; you are the Supreme Person—of this there is no doubt.
Then Śakra, mounted upon Airāvata, came into his presence. || 85–86 ||
And the Vasus, along with the Mātṛs, Thama, Varuṇa, and the Lords of Wealth, having covered the surface of the sky while stationed in their respective celestial chariots, [honored him]. || 87 ||
And at the end of the dissolution, during the creation, those who possess the nature of the Gaṇas assume the forms of Brahmā and others under the designation of the Yādava lineage. 88.

They, who shone with a brilliance equal to that of the thousand-eyed Indra, bowed down to Viśvakarman— the slayer of enemies, the Lord of all, the single-syllabled, and the imperishable— and cried out aloud.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "The Summoning of the Gaṇas," in the Skanda Purāṇa.
Sanatkumāra said:
Those lords of the Gaṇas, beings of great courage, having prostrated before the God of gods, the Lord of the lords of all gods, spoke these words: ||| 1 ||
O Blessed One, O Destroyer of the Enemies of the Gods, O Lord of Ambikā, the God of Gods!
For what purpose have we been summoned? Command us, for that [task] shall indeed be accomplished.
Shall we dry up the oceans, or shall we [bind] Yama or Rāhu with our servants?
We slay both death and time; no one exists who is unborn for him.
Having bound Indra together with the gods, including Viṣṇu and Vāyu, we shall bring him here;
or else, being greatly enraged, we shall bring the Daityas along with the Dānavas.
"Whose terrible calamity shall we bring about today by your command?
Or whose festival, O Lord, filled with the fulfillment of all desires, shall we provide?
To all those who spoke thus and bowed down, he who is affectionate toward his devotees replied:
Having honored the Gaṇas, the god Bhava, the Lord of the Gaṇas, spoke.
The God of gods said:
Listen, you who are devoted to the welfare of the world, why you have been summoned here;
having heard it, being self-restrained, perform that task without hesitation. (7)
"O lords of all lords, this Nandīśvara is our son; he is your beloved leader and your composed commander-in-chief. (8)
Therefore, all of you, acting in unison with this message of mine, consecrate him as the commander of the army, the great lord of yoga, and your husband. (9)
From this day forward, this auspicious Nandīśvara shall be your beloved, honored, and divine commander-in-chief, your lord. || 8.24.10 ||
Sanatkumāra said:
When this had been spoken by the Blessed One, all those leaders of the Gaṇas,
having deliberated and agreed, saying "So be it," then brought together the necessary materials.
Then they brought for him a divine, beautiful seat made of Jāmbūnada gold, which was as radiant as Mount Meru and enchanting to the mind.
It was also made of gold, with the luster of beautiful refined gold,
hung with strings of pearls, and illuminated by precious gems and jewels.
The pavilion, facing in all directions, was constructed with pillars made of lapis lazuli, draped with networks of tinkling bells, and adorned with fourfold red cloth.
Having fashioned a wheel in its center, they then prepared an excellent and auspicious throne;
before it was a blue footstool, radiant with diamonds.
They fashioned two jars for the purpose of supporting his feet, placed at his sides,
filled with the finest water and their openings covered with lotuses;
and having established the sacrificial fire in front, they also placed a bull at his side.
And he also [placed] the cow Surabhi, together with her calf, at his right side. || 17 ||
And he held a beautiful parasol with a hundred ribs made of Jāmbūnada gold, resplendent upon its back which was as white as a conch shell, a pearl necklace, or water. ||18||
A fan, white as the moon and with a beautiful golden handle;
and a garland of lotuses frequented by swarms of bees.
There, the leaders of the hosts brought golden *nandyāvarta* designs,
as well as two golden fish from the abode of Varuṇa, along with the *punarvasu* and *puṣya* constellations;
they also brought a golden *svastika*, a *vardhamāna*, and a *śrīvatsa*.
Kīcakas, bamboo flutes, and even maidens were highly honored.
These two elephants, Airāvata and Supratīka, are honored;
likewise, the divine banner is honored, as is the conch shell with the luster of the moon.
There is also a thousand golden jars, exceedingly radiant.
And likewise a thousand of silver vessels for the kings;
then a thousand divine copper vessels with the brilliance of fire;
and a pair of garments made from tree-bark, free from dust and exceedingly fine.
A golden crown, well-crafted by Viśvakarman, two stainless and divine earrings, and the thunderbolt, that supreme weapon. || 25 ||
The great divine *paṭṭiśa* weapon, the trident, and the thunderbolt;
a thread made of Jāmbūnada gold, and a pair of armlets;
a necklace with variegated gems, as well as yellow pigment and a golden ornament.
Nalabhā, Pāriyātra, Varṇa, and Kaṅkaṇa—
these leaders of the Gaṇas, esteemed by the gods, calmly carried from all sides sacred Darbha grass, sacrificial fuel, clarified butter, and incense. || 27-28 ||
Then the quarters, the oceans, Varuṇa..., the fire of the sky, the Vasus, and both the Moon and the Sun together with the planets [all came]. ||29||
All the stars in the form of constellations, as well as Dhruva;
the Rudras, the Rākṣasas, and the Yakṣas; the two Aśvins, the Daityas, and the Dānavas;
the Gandharvas and Apsarases, as well as Nārada and Parvata.
The earth and the oceans, the rains and the mountains,
as well as the trees, the creepers, and the mighty medicinal herbs,
and all the rivers and the Vasus from every side, assembled there. ||3.1–3.2||
The mothers of the world, as well as the earth and heaven, the elements, primordial nature, and all the sense organs in their entirety; ||33||
All sacred fords (tīrthas) and various kinds of gifts,
the Ṛg, Yajur, Sāman, and Atharvāṅgirasa Vedas,
as well as sacrifices, rituals, offerings, and religious observances— [all these are contained therein]. (34)
All the Vedic hymns, as well as the Piśācas, are divine origins.
Brahmā and the sages, as well as Viṣṇu with his followers, and those Rudras who dwell in the east, the west, the south, and likewise the north. || 3.6 ||
When all those Rudras who are below and above, as well as the Sādhyas and the Pitṛs,
had arrived, the Blessed Lord whose banner bears the bull appeared.
He commanded the Grandfather (Brahmā) to perform the entire ritual procedure:
"Having prepared each individual water-pot there, filled with all medicinal herbs,
and having filled them with water and covered them with pairs of lotuses and *kuśa* grass," || 38 ||
Jayā and Vijayā, as well as Siṃhī and Vyāghrī;
Suvarcalā, Śaṅkhapuṣpī, Viṣṇukrāntā, and Punarnavā; Kumārī, Candrakāntā, and also Mṛtasañjīvanī.
O Vyāsa, at that time, the lords of the Gaṇas cast into all the earthly beings the immortal medicinal herbs known as Ādityavarcas, Śrīniketanā, and Kumudvatī.
And within all those golden [palaces], there were various sacred fords (tīrthas). ||42||
The Blessed One established all the sacrificial gifts,
as well as the mantras and the Vedic meters, within silver jars;
likewise, he established various sacrifices involving ritual formulas, both those performed for specific desires and others.
The Blessed One, having assigned all the rivers as well as the oceans to the Audumbara vessels, and likewise having assigned the ascetic penances and religious observances,
filled each individual jar there and consecrated them with mantras.
Having wrapped it with thread, the Lord presented it to the gods;
then Brahmā himself took one jar for himself.
The Grandfather gave one to Viṣṇu and one to the wise Indra; likewise, he gave others to the Gaṇapas and to the Ṛṣis.
Then, having seated him upon that most excellent throne, the high-minded one—
Having worshipped him, Brahmā himself consecrated him;
then Viṣṇu, then Śakra, the sages along with the immortals,
and all those lords of the Gaṇas consecrated Nandin.
And that divine pair of garments, as well as divine perfumes, armlets, earrings, a crown, and even a necklace. || 8.24.50 ||
He himself gave him a spear, a trident, and a thunderbolt;
Indra, the lord of the gods, took up the umbrella, and Vāyu the fan.
And the sages, led by the Grandfather Brahmā, offered hymns of praise to him.
Viṣṇu said:
Homage to the King of Kuṣmāṇḍas, who holds a raised thunderbolt in his hand;
to the grandson of Śālaṅkāyana, who has arisen from the path of the plow. ||52||
And to the son of Śilāda, who was devoted to the chanting of the Rudra-hymns, a devotee of Rudra, a god, and one who slept within the water—salutations to him. (53)
Salutations to the Lord of the hosts, and salutations to the Lord of all beings;
to the God who is the son of Umā, and who has obtained boons from Śiva.
Salutation to the beloved son of Rudra, who bears the *paṭṭiśa* weapon;
salutation to him whose fangs are formidable and who has an eye on his forehead.
Salutations to the one who subdues, to the most excellent, to the sovereign, and to the one who is offered to;
salutations to the guardian of the gate, to the hero, to Rudra, and to the giver of boons;
salutations to the one in whom all purposes are accomplished, and salutations to the Lord of great fame.
Homage to the one who wears a supreme garland and whose abode is the ocean of milk.
To the Great Lord of the Assembly, and to the Great Master of Yoga;
to Diṇḍi and Muṇḍa, to Caṇḍa, and to the one devoted to the Single Syllable;
to the Imperishable, the Undecaying, the Ageless, and the Deathless.
Salutations to the Lord of beasts, and likewise to the conqueror of Death;
salutations to him who has the speed of the wind, the omniscient, and the unconquered;
and to him who possesses many heads and many feet.
O god who wears a crown and earrings, whose arms are like great iron clubs—protect all the hosts of gods; homage be to you!
Sanatkumāra said:
Having thus praised him, O Vyāsa, the god then, becoming composed and with palms joined in reverence, uttered the word "Victory! to that great-souled one.
Then the hosts cried "Victory!", then the gods, then the celestial beings,
then all living creatures, as well as Brahmā and Śakra.
Then [he sounded] conchs and kettledrums, as well as paṭahas and āḍambaras; flutes and cymbals, as well as kṛkavās, cow-horns,
ḍiṇḍimas, veṇukas, and mardalas in every way.
The leaders of the Gaṇas played [their instruments], filled with joy and delight.
Sanatkumāra said:
"Whoever [recites] this hymn composed by the gods for Nandīśvara..."
A mortal who recites this constantly shall go to that same world.
(66) He who performs his sleep after uttering "Namo Nandīśvarāya" shall have no fear whatsoever from the kings of the Kuṣmāṇḍas. (67)
O Vyāsa, wherever this most highly honored hymn is constantly established,
there is never any fear of the planets. Those mortals who always bow down to Nandīśvara, their senses tranquil and their being pure, [attain liberation].
They become the beloved and most excellent attendants (*gaṇas*) of the God of gods together with the Daughter of the Mountain.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Hymn of Nandīśvara," in the Skanda Purāṇa.
Sanatkumāra said:
Then, having arrived there, the god Bhava, the lord of the deities and the husband of Satī, honored the Maruts and spoke to them regarding the maiden.
The Lord, together with Śakra and Pitāmaha, addressed by name those Maruts who possess great speed, great courage, and great power:
"Your daughter Suyashā, who is virtuous and possesses a divine form— " || 2 ||
"Having honored her, you ought to give her [to us]; she shall become our daughter-in-law.
The Maruts said:
"She belongs to us, to her [husband], and likewise to the entire world."
O powerful Lord of the three worlds, you ought not to ask us [for anything].
You alone should give and you alone should receive; you are our unsurpassed refuge.
Do not treat us as strangers by making such a request.
Our father is the illustrious Kaśyapa, and Marīci is our grandfather;
Brahmā is the grandfather of our grandfather, and you, O Great One, are even his father.
Thus, you are our great-grandfather; it does not behove you to treat us as strangers.
Ishvara said:
"You are not our enemies; what has been spoken to you is the truth.
However, it was spoken by the sages and gods for the sake of the welfare of the world."
"A maiden who has not been given away must not be taken; this is the eternal dharma.
Sanatkumāra said:
Having been addressed thus by the Maruts, the best of gods, the Lord of the Gods—
At that very moment, he brought Suyaśas, the daughter of the Maruts.
There, he himself was the Hotṛ priest; the Grandfather of the Worlds was the Brahmā; Kaśyapa was the Udgātṛ, and Atri sang the Sāman hymn himself. (8–9)
The two gods Atharvan and Aṅgiras also performed the office of the Brahman priest;
as did Nārada, Parvata, and the singer Citrasena, as well as Viśvāvasu, Ruci, Hāhā, and Hūhū. || 8.25.10 ||
Likewise, Śāliśiras, the renowned Gaṇḍamaṇḍaka,
Īti, Indravāha, Yajñavāha, and Dakṣiṇa—
these and other Gandharvas with sweet voices sang. || 11-12 ||
Urvaśī, Rambhā, Ghṛtācī, Pūrvacitti,
Tilottamā, Viśvācī, and other apsarases likewise—
those highly fortunate ones— danced a dance most enchanting to the gods.
Sanatkumāra said: O Vyāsa, such was the incomparable and irreproachable wedding of that wise Nandin, the chief of the Gaṇas. || 16 ||
Then, having performed the marriage ceremony, the high-minded Nandin went and prostrated at the feet of the God, the Goddess, and Brahmā;
and the lord of the world, endowed with supreme splendor, also paid homage to Śilāda.
The God of gods said:
"Choose a boon, my son, and you too, O dear daughter-in-law.
I shall grant you boons, my child, whatever you desire in your heart. (18)
Nandi said:
"O Blessed One, if you are pleased, let my devotion to you be firm;
and may you, together with Ambā and the Lord of the Gaṇas, always remain well-disposed toward me. (19)
"O God, O Lord, O Giver of Desires, you ought to unite this father of mine with a favor endowed with grace.
The God of Gods said:
O wise Nandīśa, lord of the Gaṇas, I am always well-pleased with you, together with Pārvatī; now hear these words of mine.
He is desired by all, most excellent, endowed with supreme sovereignty;
he is a great yogi, a mighty archer, and possessed of great strength and prowess. || 22 ||
Be forever unconquerable and a conqueror, worthy of worship and a worshipper;
wherever I am, there you shall be, and wherever you are, there I shall also be.
He who hates you hates me; he who follows you follows me.
And this father of yours, my son, is endowed with supreme sovereignty.
He shall become my leader of the hosts, Mahāgaṇapati.
And I grant him the Vaibhrāja celestial chariot, which moves at will, is made entirely of gold,
and is filled with divine mansions and surrounded by attendants.
Therefore, he shall wander through all the worlds as he desires. ||26||
And his place shall be well-honored on Śrīparvata;
and that righteous man who gives up his life at that Bhṛgu shall become a leader of the Gaṇas in Vaibhrāja, moving according to his will. ||27||
Sanatkumāra said:
Then the highly fortunate goddess chose a boon from Śailādi;
he replied, "May my devotion toward you always remain unfailing."
Then the daughter of Marut, urged by both of them,
replied to them as follows:
"May I have devotion to you two, and likewise to my husband."
"May my supreme resolve toward the Dharma be eternal and never depart from me.
O Lords of Gods, grantors of thousands of boons, I desire this boon.
Sanatkumāra said:
Then, O lady of pure smiles, those two gods, filled with joy, said to that woman of excellent complexion, the daughter-in-law: "From him alone shall this be yours.
Having gazed upon Nārāyaṇa and Brahmā, Hara likewise spoke.
"From this day forward, Nandīśa shall always be honored by you both;
indeed, through his lordship over the gods, he shall serve as your doorkeeper. O Nandinī, whatever devotion and affection you possess toward me, let that same [devotion] be yours."
"Let it be so, O Lord of Gods; there is no need for further deliberation here.
Then all the Gaṇas, desiring to do what was pleasing to the God, approached him. Those beings of great courage granted him a boon, and he, who possessed a golden luster, chose his reward.
My devotion to you and my sovereignty are likewise esteemed;
you are all worthy of my veneration, and I am dear to you alone. || 3.6 ||
The Gaṇas said:
"You are the restrainer and the permitter, the goal and the means of arrival;
you are the lord of us all and the sovereign even of the gods. (37)
You are the most excellent among the Kuṣmāṇḍas, you are the one of great strength among the Rudras,
and likewise the gatekeeper of the calamities as well as of the Pramathas.
You are indeed considered by us to be the one of great strength, the great yogin, and our commander;
you are the being and the leader of beings, the guide and the supreme leader.
You are the sovereign of the planets and likewise the wielder of Rudra’s staff.

You are the foremost warrior, the slayer of enemies; you are the hero and the lord of heaven. You are indeed possessed of great majesty, the abode of the Ocean of Milk, the sanctuary of Japyeśvara, and one who is manifested by Japyeśvara.
The creator of all beings, the giver of boons, who is himself worshipped by the givers of boons—
O Lord, Sovereign of Beings, become for us as well a granter of boons.
Sanatkumāra said:
Thus praised by all the leaders of the Gaṇas, the lord Nandīśvara spoke to them as they bowed before him: "Tell me, what shall I do for you?
When they were thus addressed, all those leaders of the Gaṇas, who were possessed of great strength, [spoke].
Those who knew his divine nature spoke to him in the presence of the God of gods:
"You have been made the leader of our host by Lord Śambhu;
you have been consecrated by us as our chief and bestower of righteousness. ||44-45||
Therefore, being auspicious and gentle, possessed of virtues even amidst those devoid of virtue, and endowed with patience, purity, and self-restraint, always act for our benefit. ||46||
Sanatkumāra said:
Having been addressed thus, he then bowed to all with great reverence;
placing his joined palms upon his head, he then praised the leaders of the Gaṇas.
Nandin said:
"Homage to you all, O beings; homage indeed to the yogis as well;
and homage also to the homeless ones, the lords of yogis—homage, homage! (48)
Homage to those who move at will and homage indeed to the fierce ones;
homage again and again to the Deaths, to the Yamās, and to the Times. Homage to those with golden garlands and to all the Dharmas.
Homage to you who inflict death and likewise to those who are not to be slain;
homage to the supreme yogis and homage again and again to those with matted hair.
Homage to you whose forms are visible and likewise to those who are transformed.
Salutations to those clothed in bark garments and indeed to those clad in animal skins;
salutations to those wearing white robes and garlands, and repeated salutations to those with variegated garlands.
Salutations again and again to those who are running, to those who are galloping, and to those who are standing still.
Homage to the sages who sing and those who recite; homage, homage!
Homage to those in the form of śarabhas and to those in the form of śatās;
homage to those in the form of mountains and to those in the form of tigers.

Homage to those in the form of cats, and likewise to crows and owls; homage to those in the form of deities, and similarly to the winds; homage to the fires, as well as to the waters and to the Varuṇas.
Homage to those who have the form of the Lord of Wealth, and indeed to those of every form;
homage to those with bellies for faces, and indeed to those with faces everywhere; homage to those of dwarf-like forms, and indeed to those who can assume any form at will.
Salutations again and again to those who provide nourishment for gods, asuras, and humans;
salutations to you all gods, salutations to you who are auspicious from every side.
May there be salutations to you, the planets, and likewise salutations to you, the liberations.
"Salutations be to you who are auspicious, and likewise to those who are inauspicious.
May the leaders of the hosts (gaṇanāyakas) be gentle and auspicious toward me.
Thus were the mighty lords of the hosts (gaṇapatis) praised.
May those destroyers of the enemies of the gods, through their auspicious words, grant me incomparable happiness; may they, the bestowers of bliss,
grant me strength, valor, and steadfastness in battle.
May they grant me the destruction of my sins, a stable station, incomparable progress, as well as great fame, constant adherence to Dharma,
and everything desired by my mind.
Likewise, the lords of the gods [bestowed] unsurpassed nourishment. ||61||
Sanatkumāra said:
He who constantly recites these two hymns to the lords of the hosts of Nandins becomes one who has performed the final purificatory bath of a horse sacrifice and is liberated from all sins.
By reciting [the mantra] during the latter twilight, one casts off the sin committed during the day;
and by reciting it during the former twilight, one likewise casts off everything committed during the night. (63)
Sanatkumāra said: Then all those leaders of the Gaṇas, having been thus praised by that wise one,
were dismissed and departed after bowing down to the bull-bannered Lord.
Then the gods and all the worlds, as well as the high-minded god Bhava himself,
having created the abode of Nandīśvara, bestowed it upon him.
Together with the Goddess, he indeed went to that imperishable abode which is his desire;
[he who hears] this birth of Nandin, as well as the granting of the boon.
Whether he recites or causes others to hear [this account of] the consecration and the marriage,
that Brāhmaṇa, upon death, attains the same world as Nandīśvara.
But he who, with a restrained mind and full of devotion to Bhava, recites all this with humility, even he, departing for the next world, becomes an attendant equal to Nandi. || 68 ||
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Great Fortune of Nandikeśvara," in the Skanda Purāṇa.
Sanatkumāra said:
O Vyāsa, in this manner Nandīśvara was born as an attendant.
He was consecrated as the commander-in-chief of the God of Gods.
Vyāsa said:
Then, seated there with the Goddess, what did the Blessed One, the Great God who grants all desires, do? This I wish to know.
Sanatkumāra said: On a peak of the Himavat mountains, the Blessed Lord Śarva, desiring to please the Goddess,
repeatedly produced laughter through his variously shaped attendants.
The Lord, who bears the crescent moon as his forehead mark, delighted and sported with the Goddess,
accompanied by auspicious beings of great power, omniscient, and capable of assuming any form at will.
Then the Supreme Goddess approached her mother alone.
She saw the virtuous goddess Satī, of auspicious form, arrived and seated upon a splendid, highly honored golden throne;
he then honored that blameless lady with a most precious seat.
And as she was seated, Menā, the beloved of Himavat, said to her:
"O daughter of auspicious gaze, it has indeed been a long time since your arrival today.
Your husband is now sporting together with you using the toys of the poor."
Those who were once poor and likewise without refuge—
O auspicious lady, both of them now sport in this manner, just as your husband does.
Sanatkumāra said: Having been addressed thus by her mother, she was not at all joyful in mind;
possessed of great forbearance, she said nothing to her at all.
Then, having been dismissed by her mother, she went and spoke to the God:
"O Blessed One, Lord of the Gods, I shall not dwell here on this mountain;
O Lord of the World, O You of Great Splendor, choose another abode for me."
The God of Gods said: O Sovereign Goddess, though you were constantly urged by me for the sake of a dwelling place, you never once, O Devi, took pleasure in residing elsewhere.
"Now, O beautiful one, why do you yourself seek to dwell elsewhere? Tell me that, O goddess of pure smiles. (12)
The Goddess said:
"O Lord of Gods, today I went to the house of my high-souled father;
and there, in a secluded place, I beheld my mother, the creator of the worlds. (13)
Having honored her with a seat and other offerings, she spoke to me thus:
"O Umā, O auspicious one, your husband always plays with the toys of the poor."
Indeed, the play of the gods is not of such a kind as this,
O Mahādeva; that you take delight with those various auspicious attendants is truly distasteful to me and my mother, O Bull-bannered One.
Sanatkumāra said: Then the Lord, the Master, laughed and spoke to the Goddess in order to make her smile: "It is even so; there is no doubt. Why did anger arise in you?"
Clad in a hide or indeed naked, he dwells in cremation grounds;
homeless, he resides in forests and in the caves of mountains.
"I wander surrounded by hosts of naked ones, O lotus-eyed one!
Do not be angry, O Goddess; you are my mother. Your mother spoke the truth to you: for there is no kinsman equal to a mother for living beings, O beautiful one. (18)
The Goddess said: "O Lord of the foremost of gods, I have no business with my kinsmen.
O Mahādeva, act in such a way that we may dwell elsewhere."
Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the Goddess, the Lord of Gods, the Sovereign and Master,
spoke to the leader of his hosts standing at his side, the renowned one named Nikumbha.
O Nikumbha, lord of the Gaṇas, go to the auspicious Vārāṇasī and make it empty by means of stratagem alone, O mighty-armed one, not by force.
There dwells the powerful King Divodāsa,
who is righteous, devoted to me, a great yogi, and possessed of great strength.
Go there and act in such a way that you do not offend him.
"And by his very transgression, make Vārāṇasī empty.
Sanatkumāra said:
"O best of the Gaṇas, having been addressed thus, the radiant Nikumbha—"
Bowing down with joined palms and a joyful countenance, he spoke to the God:
"O Lord of Gods, I shall act in such a way that this king will become the sovereign of the Aparas, and you, O Lord, will be gratified."
"Vārāṇasī itself will undoubtedly become empty.
Sanatkumāra said:
Having spoken thus, Nikumbha bowed his head to Hara.
The Lord went to the holy city of Vārāṇasī, renowned throughout the worlds.
There, that Gaṇa appeared to Maṇḍūkākṣa the barber in a dream and revealed his own true form to him at that time.
Nikumbha said: "O Maṇḍūkākṣa, I am Nikumbha, the leader of the Gaṇas and the destroyer of grief.
I have come here to bestow grace upon you; do whatever I tell you. (28)
Establish my abode at the gate of Divodāsa’s house, and install there an auspicious image that resembles my own form. (29)
I shall grant you wealth, as well as sons and good fortune; moreover, I shall grant you popularity everywhere and, finally, the supreme state.
Sanatkumāra said:
Having been addressed thus by Nikumbha, the barber then went to King Divodāsa—who was like Indra or Vaivasvata—and spoke to him. (31)
The barber said: "Master, I shall fashion a Gaṇapālaya at your house door;
I will install Gaṇeśa there, so you ought to grant me permission for this. (32)
Saying "So be it," he was granted permission and then constructed a temple there;
he installed an image exactly as he had seen it,
and he established a grand and beautiful ritual for its worship.
That great being, Gaṇeśa, accepted it from him.
Sanatkumāra said:
By that deed, whatever wealth he desired was granted to him.
Indeed, the Lord bestowed cattle, sons, and good fortune. ||35||
Having observed that barber's incomparable prosperity,
the people, desiring to please him, indeed performed worship for him.
Some performed pilgrimages, while others observed fasts; likewise, some offered oblations and recited prayers, and others performed worship for the sake of obtaining boons.
Similarly, some presented offerings, while others engaged in song and dance.
To them who had thus approached him, the highly illustrious Nikumbha granted every desire that each of them wished for. Then,
King Divodāsa, realizing that he was a granter of such wishes, [acted accordingly].
O Vyāsa, once the queen said [to him] out of a desire for a son:
"O Goddess, this one grants all the desires of people;
you too should propitiate this Lord of the Gaṇas for the sake of offspring."
Having been addressed thus, that beautiful woman then went and approached Gaṇeśa, and said:
"O Blessed One, O Lord, O God, I am childless;
I shall observe a fast for the propitiation of you, O God."
"I shall not eat until a boon has been granted to me by you, O Lord;
once a son is born, I will give ten times ten hundreds. (43)

O Lord of the hosts of cows, with reference to you, I shall perform for you a ceremonial bath among the twice-born with a thousand jars of curd, clarified butter, milk, and the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). 44.
"When a son is born to you, I shall undoubtedly feed a hundred thousand Brahmins, well-honored, before you. (45)
The king will grant you many villages as well as female slaves, O Lord; he will always perform sacrificial sessions and offer worship to you. ||46||
Sanatkumāra said:
O Vyāsa, having spoken thus to him, she remained established in her observance;
fasting at that time, she performed a great worship of him.
To her who was standing thus, that lord of the Gaṇas, the god, said:
"Arise; you shall have no son; do not indulge in vain grief. (48)
Thus, though she was repeatedly addressed by that high-souled Gaṇeśa Nikumbha, she desisted from her vow;
then the goddess, dejected in mind, spoke to the lord of men.
"Noble son, this Gaṇapa does not give me a son;
he says, 'You have no son,' so do not practice vows in vain. (8.26.50)
Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the queen, that lord of men, the king, remained constantly observant of his vows before Gaṇeśa. ||5.1||
Nikumbha spoke to that king who was established in his vow:
"O King, do not remain here in vain; I will not give you a son. (52)
Thus addressed by Nikumbha, that mighty lord of kings,
his eyes red with anger, rose up and spoke to the lord of the Gaṇas.
The king said:
Whether you are a *gaṇa*, a *piśāca*, a *bhūta*, or even a *rākṣasa*, you are undoubtedly ungrateful; you do not deserve worship here.
Yet, you have been honored by the citizens right at the door of my house.
"You dwell within my domain, yet you do not grant me a son;
therefore, you are unworthy of honor and deserve punishment from me.
You are cruel, arrogant, harsh, and filled with envy. || 55-56 ||
Sanatkumāra said:
Then he caused his dwelling to be broken down by leaders of elephant herds;
he quickly demolished the sacrificial altar and burned the radiant image.
The lord Nikumbha, having achieved his purpose, remained stationed in the sky and spoke to Divodāsa as if burning him with his splendor:
"The gods grant whatever desired boon one wishes for."
If that anger had not been given away, what would have become of you in that situation? (59)
"Since you have destroyed the home of me, who have done you no harm, therefore your city shall remain empty for a thousand years. (8.26.60)
Sanatkumāra said: Having thus spoken to the king, Nikumbha, who was possessed of the supreme self,
informed the Lord of the Gods in this manner and stood by the side of the Master.
Then the king, having reached a state of extreme shame because of his words which were indeed true in their meaning, returned to his palace.
Then, by that curse, the city of Vārāṇasī quickly became empty, purified, and frequented by deer.
But perceiving that [palace] to be empty, the wielder of the Pināka bow, endowed with great splendor, arrived there together with the Goddess, his attendants, and Nandin.
There he beheld a divine celestial chariot, radiant as the sun, which was his own mental creation.
The Lord created the incomparable quality by means of his mind alone.
Sanatkumāra said:
"My wisdom is not sufficient to describe that in its entirety."
This much can be said: for that [garden] possesses incomparable qualities.
The Lord created a glorious garden that was far superior even to those delightful celestial gardens, such as Nandana and the rest. || 67 ||

In that celestial chariot, endowed with every supernatural power and beyond the reach of words, the Goddess, whose eyes were like blooming blue lotuses, took her delight; she no longer remembered the words of her own mother.
Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Emptying of Vārāṇasī," in the Skanda Purāṇa.
Sanatkumāra said: Then, Śiva and Pārvatī, the daughter of the mountain, were seated comfortably upon a divine golden throne adorned with various jewels.
Then the goddess, the daughter of Acala, seated comfortably during the night,
the daughter of the Lord of Mountains, spoke to her husband, the Lord of all the worlds:
"O Blessed One, O slayer of the enemies of the gods, O you who are adorned by a portion of the moon!"
O Lord, O giver of honor, tell me this which I ask of you. || 3 ||
O Lord of Gods, O you who are affectionate toward your devotees, what fruit do those obtain who perform even that which is nothing at all for the sake of a reward? (4)
Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by Umā, the trident-bearing god whose banner is the bull,
the God of gods, remained composed and spoke of all that is auspicious and inauspicious.
Vyāsa said:
What did that blessed Lord, the god of great asceticism and the imperishable one, say when he was thus affectionately questioned by the goddess?
Sanatkumāra said:
O Vyāsa, O Brahmin, I too formerly questioned the lord Nandīśvara; I shall relate to you exactly what he told me.
I, being composed, questioned the lord of the Gaṇas, the heroic Nandīśvara, who possessed the splendor of ten thousand suns and was exceedingly radiant.
"O best of the Gaṇas, tell me according to the truth that which was previously spoken by Īśa to the Goddess; for my curiosity is indeed great.
Nandin said:
Listen, O great sage, as I shall relate to you that which was spoken of old by the God of gods to Pārvatī when she questioned him.
The God of gods said:
Listen, O lady of virtuous vows, for I shall declare that which you ask of me.
O Goddess, being questioned, I shall tell it to you for the benefit of my devotees.
O blameless Goddess, whoever would grant me a pure favor—
I ordain for him a house in Śivapura that shall be imperishable, O Arjuna.
Whoever establishes my linga according to the prescribed injunctions as described,
he moves eternally with me, endowed with the eightfold supernatural powers.
Whoever would give to me even a mere trifle of gold, or a great amount, [attains the same].
Upon its snowy peak, I grant him an excellent dwelling.
"To whoever would give me a cow or gold with a joyful heart for my pleasure,
I shall grant him worlds endowed with all desires;
and likewise to him who gives me a bull, whether white or even blue."
He shall deliver twenty-one generations of his family on both sides.
Or, he who gives me land as large as two cow-hides,
having reached my city, rejoices together with the lords of the Gaṇas.
Whoever should give me the fruit of merit previously acquired by themselves, that person obtains infinite fruit and rejoices in the third heaven. || 18 ||
He who performs my funeral procession on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight in a chariot yoked with bulls rejoices in my world.
To him who worships me with honors, services, and recitations of prayers,
I grant a highly honored residence in the world of Brahmā.
And he who, even in his mind, should think, "I shall worship Hara"— [he too attains that same state].
O slender-waisted one, for him who is incapable and possesses no wealth, there is no [obstacle];
purified by that faith and liberated from all sins,
he attains my world upon the dissolution of the body— of this there is no doubt.
He who, having bathed during the morning twilight, always approaches me,
becomes a powerful Yakṣa, a friend of the King of Yakṣas.
Sweeping [the temple] five hundred times and smearing it with cow-dung a thousand times—
Ten thousand perfumes and infinite worship are prescribed;
there should be one hundred and eight anointments and three hundred ablutions.
There should likewise be five hundred offerings of scented water and five hundred of the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). || 24–25 ||
O Goddess, milk should be five times that amount, and Kapila [cow's milk] even more than that;
likewise, the bath with clarified butter (sarpiḥ) should again be five times that.
O Goddess, I forgive her many offenses.
The consecration with ashes, the infinite, and the secret, O my beloved.
Ten thousand units of aguru, six thousand of sandalwood,
and fourteen thousand of black aloe-wood incense are prescribed.
Rice and barley are considered inexhaustible, while śāli rice is prescribed at two hundred units.
Ānantya and guggulu, when well-incensed with clarified butter—
O Goddess, he who burns two thousand palas of mahiṣākṣa for a full year shall become equal to Nandin. || 29 || || 30 ||
He who, for one year, offers milk-rice with ghee to the auspicious southern form shall become equal to Nandin.

There were ten thousand sacrificial cakes (caru) and four times as many barley-gruel offerings (yāvaka); all the remaining sacrificial cakes were equal to half the number of the barley-gruel offerings.
An incalculable vessel of clarified butter here and eternally in the hereafter;
it gratifies all the ancestors, and one rejoices in a celestial chariot.
He who gives an umbrella and a collection of banners after having beautified them, he too shines forth intensely in the sky with splendor, like the sun. (34)
On both the thirteenth and the eighth days of the lunar fortnight,
one who observes a fast should worship me with devotion and offerings, O blameless lady.
"O Goddess, being pleased, I grant him my own eternal realm.
Since I have always been worshipped with devotion by means of red and yellow garments as well as various flowers, I ordain him to be my son. (36)
And to that mortal who, remaining steadfast, maintains a lamp for a single night, we grant the fruit of all sacrifices as well as prosperity itself. (37)
All the worlds, including both the ignorant and the learned, are deluded by me alone;
blinded by passion and thickened by darkness, they do not perceive me.
Those who are meditative, disciplined in yoga, devoted to the true Dharma, single-minded, and self-controlled—they behold me eternally. (39)
Those who are my devotees and are always proficient in Sāṃkhya and Yoga perceive everything in Me, and through Yoga they perceive Me everywhere.
Having transcended the three worlds as well as the world of Brahmā,
they go to my own realm, having pierced through the darkness that is so difficult to pierce.
I cannot be seen even by hosts of sages endowed with asceticism;
O Goddess, only the wise who are meditators and ever-disciplined behold me. 42.
And having performed all these actions, O beautiful one, with a perfectly tranquil mind and a compassionate heart, do not [act otherwise]. (43)
By bestowing a gift of gold and land upon a Brahmin while thinking, "May Rudra be pleased with me," one indeed enjoys incomparable fruit. ||44||
O fair-hipped one, whatever holy fords and shrines of the deities exist in the worlds, they are always present at my feet. (45)
Likewise, they stood with their right hands upon the hands of the Brahmins;
he who sees me as all-pervading and sees everything as being in me—||46||
With his mind perpetually offered unto Me and thus permeated by My nature, he is liberated from all sins through My very power. 47.
O Goddess, in every way, even while engaged in worldly activity, the man who always remembers me shall never be joined with impurity,
O doer, even if he is in any state whatsoever and possesses a sinful nature, provided his mind is steeped in the sleep of knowledge.
Whoever constantly worships me shall become equal to my own self.
And whoever should always worship me with the sixfold yoga, he shall quickly enter into me; there is no doubt in this matter. (8.27.50)

O Goddess, even one who delights in the company of the wicked, who is born of a low womb, and who is constantly possessed of sinful deeds— even he, if his mind is fixed on me and he offers himself to me, attains an inconceivable state.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, "The Ritual for the Worship of Īśvara," in the Skanda Purāṇa.
Sanatkumāra said:
Then, O Vyāsa, the auspicious Goddess again addressed her husband, the lord of vows.
Honored by hundreds of fruits, she asked about the fruit associated with the vow.
O Lord of the Three Worlds, O Maheśvara, tell me what the fruit of vows is— whether it be small or great— and of whatever kind a vow may be.
The God of Gods said: "O auspicious one, O blameless lady, listen to me regarding what vow has been proclaimed—whether it yields great fruit or even small fruit. (3)
On the fourteenth and eighth days of both fortnights, being pure,
abstaining from food for a year, peaceful, self-controlled, and having conquered his senses— ||4||
Whatever fruit belongs to one who performs a long sacrificial session (sattra) and to those who speak the truth and approach their wives during the proper seasons—
that very fruit he obtains, and he does not see Yama.
He who has taken refuge in me, yet remains on his bed or seat in the midst of women, attached to pleasure and delighting in ease—he burns constantly from the very tips of his nails. (6)
My devotee, endowed with austerity, attains Me alone;
his worlds are imperishable, O Goddess, even if he should be a doer of evil.
O Goddess, that man who always eats from an earthen vessel on the sacred festival days (parvan) obtains the fruit of a three-night fast by means of a single day and night. ||8||
He who, indeed, for one year eats daily without weariness,
having offered [the food] to the ancestors and the gods, shall become the sole sovereign of the earth.
O Goddess, the man who eats on these holy days—the ninth, the eighth, the full moon, and the thirteenth—for an entire year, [incurs great sin]. (8.28.10)
O blameless one, he attains lordship over the Gaṇas without rival;
he becomes beloved by all beings and assumes a divine form. || 1.1 ||
One should offer a śrīvatsa mark made with flour and an auspicious golden fruit;
one should scatter black sesame seeds there, as well as rice grains and unbroken rice (akṣata),
along with various kinds of flavorful fruits as they may be obtained.
He indeed rejoices in heaven for sixty-two thousand years,
assuming a divine form and endowed with splendor, forever together with the deities—
[he who would give me his own image made of *hirivera*]. 13–14.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, [one should offer] food well-prepared with all kinds of perfumes and juices, along with various types of hard and soft foods.
And here, on the eastern and southern sides, as well as on the western and northern sides,
one should place yellow orpiment, black agallochum, and realgar.
One should indeed offer sandalwood, duly honored according to the sequence;
O Goddess Mattakāśinī, hear from me what the fruit of that merit is. 17.
Completely freed from all diseases and likewise stainless,
having enjoyed great happiness in heaven for eight hundred million years,
he is born happy in this world and attains me alone.
Whether a Brāhmaṇa, a Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya, a Śūdra, a woman, or even a man, whoever should give a string of jewels (ratnāvalī) attains supreme happiness like mine in my world. Furthermore,
one should offer white mustard seeds (siddhārthaka) with the Aghora mantra, whether in a rite for the gods or for the ancestors.
He shall gratify the ancestors for thirty thousand years,
as well as the sages and all the gods; he attains a magnificent form and is honored by the daughters of the cows in Goloka for the duration of a Manvantara.

All the gods, as well as Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and the sages, indeed establish their presence within the arghya; for it has issued forth from them. O Goddess, he who knows this supreme secret is a man of great austerity.
By its power, one shall become wealthy and pleasing to behold,
endowed with wisdom, beauty, and virtue, and live for a hundred years.
He who, being diligent, bathes me constantly three times a day with milk—

I shall forgive even a thousand offenses of that person. Furthermore, whoever beholds that ceremonial bathing shall be liberated from those sins and shall obtain the fruit of a thousand mental recitations.
But he who, being pure, performs the ritual bathing with milk for one year,
attains the status of a leader of the Gaṇas and constant favor.
The man who, with an undistracted mind, performs an anointing for me with clarified butter,
shall obtain the fruit of two thousand mental recitations;
that best of men shall also become worthy of being approached by the gods.
One shall obtain the fruit of a thousand gold coins (*niṣka*).
To him who performs the sweeping while observing the vow for a full year,
I grant the auspicious world, which is eternally and certainly blissful.
O Īśvarī, even when all the worlds perish, there is no destruction for him;
O Goddess, so too for one who, firm in his vow, performs the worship of my linga. ||3.1||
For a hundred thousand divine years, he rejoices in heaven;
Śaṅkara smells the fragrance of four kinds of flowers. ||32||
O Goddess, it is said that for every flower— whether of the *arka*, *karavīra*, *bilva*, or *baka*— it is equivalent to a gold *niṣka*.
Furthermore, the fruit that is said to be obtained when a thousand *arka* flowers are offered is [attained].
Indeed, when even a single flower of the *karavīra* is offered, that is its fruit.
Whatever fruit may result from giving a thousand karavīra flowers,
that same fruit is said to result from giving a single lotus.
Whatever fruit is obtained from giving a thousand lotuses to me, that same fruit one obtains by offering a beautiful leaf of the *bilva* tree. ||36||
Whatever fruit is traditionally said to be obtained by giving a thousand bilva leaves to me, one obtains that same fruit by giving a single bakapuṣpa flower to me. (37)
Whatever fruit is obtained from giving me a thousand *bakapuṣpa* flowers, one obtains that same fruit by giving a single *dhattūra* flower. (38)
For whoever shall constantly bear my floral remains (*nirmālya*) upon their head—
even if that person is impure, one who has broken the bounds of propriety, a man possessed of sin,
self-willed, liberated from [all] restraints, or cast outside the pale of discipline— [he shall attain the highest state]. (39)
He shall fall into a terrible hell and be reborn among the animal species. ||8.28.40||
O observer of great vows, if one who has become pure and practices celibacy wears my floral remains (nirmālya), I shall swiftly destroy his sin.
He who indeed offers a garland of lamps to me during the month of Kārttika,
being pure, should at the conclusion of the lamp-offering gratify the Brāhmaṇas.
He attains the status of a leader of the Gaṇas and shines like the sun;
he should also give black sesame seeds along with white mustard seeds.
O Goddess, whoever always places [these] upon my head shall become equal to Nandin;
for those which are called *siddhārthaka* as well as those black sesame seeds— 44.
O Goddess, all of them are composed of you; this is the secret declared by me.
[He] rejoices together with my host named Citra. (46)
And when the universal dissolution has arrived and the destruction of the three worlds occurs,
having abandoned all sufferings, he attains me alone.

O Goddess, daughter of the mountain, I am not as well-pleased by being worshipped with ritual offerings as I am exceedingly satisfied when the *liṅga* is worshipped, O Pārvatī. Whether one is attached to all the senses or joined with all sins, [I am pleased by the worship of the *liṅga*].
O Goddess, he who worships my Liṅga here goes to heaven;
having abandoned all sins, free from the pairs of opposites, with his impurities burnt away, eating my remnants and offering salutations to me, he attains me alone. (8.28.49–50)
Sanatkumāra said:
Then the Blessed Lady again questioned her husband, the Lord of all the worlds: "O God, by what means may you flourish, and with what are you satisfied?"
Then, with a smiling face, the Blessed One, the Lord of the lords of all worlds,
spoke these words out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds:
The God of gods said:
Listen, O Goddess of auspicious countenance, to the truth of how all living beings in the three worlds who are my devotees attain a blessed state. (53)
Whatever is that most supreme secret, all of that abides in me;
for whoever knows it in its true essence is liberated from cyclic existence. ||54||
A person should not reveal this secret; rather, having risen in the morning with palms joined in reverence, he should always recite my name as "Sarvasaha.
By that recitation, he shall utterly burn away every sin.
Having attained fame and renown, he is glorified in the world of Rudra. ||56||
Whoever should constantly offer all kinds of garlands upon my forms,
according to the rules and with the mantra, his meritorious fruit shall be great.
(57) The Mantra:
Salutations always to the omnipresent Lord of the gods, who consists of all the deities; salutations indeed to the Blessed One, the secret of secrets;
salutations to Soma, the Lord of beings, the creator, and Bhava.
Svāhā indeed to the All-Secret, and to the One Consisting of the Secrets of the Gods;
the mantra consisting of all secrets, svāhā, and also to Soma;
svāhā indeed to Kaṭaṅkaṭa, and svāhā to the Mighty God.
Whoever should daily offer flowers with this mantra,
by him a thousand recitations of the mental [mantra] will have been performed.
Then, on the new moon day, one who is well-composed should join his palms in añjali until they are completely full.
O Pārvatī, having worshipped black sesame seeds and mustard seeds according to the rule and as they are available, one should offer them while uttering these words: "Sūrya" and "Va-mama. (62–63)
Freed from all sins, that man shall go to the heavenly world;
and having worshipped me, O Goddess, he should also gratify the Brāhmaṇas with food.
He does not obtain that fruit, nor indeed am I pleased with him who,
having worshipped the twice-born and me, should recite my names.
Furthermore, O Goddess, on the fourteenth and the eighth days of both fortnights, he too shall be liberated; he does not go to a womb-less state.
Or again, [he may recite] "Vāmadeva," "Sudeva," or "Hara Gupta."
"O Lord of Umā, O Blue-throated One, O Peaceful One, O Śrīkaṇṭha, O Lord of Rays!
O Śarva, O Bhīma, O Paśupati, O Śaṅkara, O Ugra, O Bhava!"—thus proclaiming these names, as well as another secret name, "Mahādeva. || 67–68 ||
One shall be liberated from all sins and honored by the gods in heaven;
whoever should either recite or cause even one of these to be recited,
having shattered the path of the body, he attains me alone.
Thus, whatever has been proclaimed by me regarding all forms of prostration, [is now concluded]. ||8.28.70||
Whoever constantly burns guggulu resin mixed with clarified butter and milk on the new moon day—this is my secret and is dear to me;
by my grace, he attains the imperishable station, of this there is no doubt. (71)
And whoever, O Goddess, should communicate this supreme secret to me, [he shall attain success]. || 72 ||
Having offered a full vessel filled with *arka* leaves, along with ghee and honey, according to the prescribed rite and with devotion, one is liberated from all sins. ||73||
And, O highly fortunate one, whoever should proclaim these names of mine—
[I am] one whose abode is the cremation ground, naked, lying in ashes, firm in my vows;
Vāmadeva, the tranquil, the one with a stiffened phallus, the three-eyed one.
He is dear to the left, he is the left, he possesses many forms, and he is the end-maker of the end-maker. ||75||
He is the Ancient One, the one invoked by many, the death of death, and the conqueror of the senses;
he is beyond the senses, yet possesses super-sensory power, and dwells in the hearts of all beings.
He is the wheel of saṃsāra, the soul of yoga, the bearer of the skull, and indeed Diṇḍi.

One who possesses self-restraint should mutter "Mahādeva, Mahādeva, Mahādeva," or likewise listen to this constantly. Upon the dissolution of the body, he shall become a leader of the Gaṇas, his very self being Yoga.
Sanatkumāra said: A devoted person should never recite this to one who is inauspicious, nor to a sinner, nor to one who is untruthful or devoid of vows, nor to one who is lacking in merit.

It is auspicious, conducive to fame and long life, a bringer of peace and prosperity, beautiful, pure, supremely sacred, and the most auspicious of all auspicious things. It should not be heard by everyone, nor should it be given to anyone at all. ||81||
Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, titled "The Worship of Īśvara," in the Skanda Purāṇa.
Vyāsa said: Having thus reached his dwelling in Vārāṇasī in the course of time...
What could the two gods, the parents of the world, have done beyond this?
Sanatkumāra said:
Then that blessed Lord [addressed] the goddess, the daughter of Himavat.
He said, "O Queen, let us go see the garden, if it pleases you."
The Goddess said:
"So be it, O Lord of Gods, just as you have spoken, O Bull-bannered One! Indeed, O Hara, one must not go beyond this garden."
Sanatkumāra said:
Then, O Vyāsa, the Bull-bannered Lord, together with the Goddess, wandered everywhere in Vārāṇasī for the sake of desiring to see the divine [sights]. 4.
In that eastern direction, the god who wields the Pināka bow showed the goddess a garden adorned with various kinds of flowers.
It was crowded with *campaka*, *aśoka*, *punnāga*, *priyaṅgu*, and mango trees,
as well as *bilva*, *arjuna*, and *kadamba* trees, and also *nyagrodha* and *udumbara* trees;
it was further filled with fragrant blossoms such as *jātī*, *kesara*, and *ketaka*.
With delightful, fragrant flowers frequented by swarms of bees.
Having reached that garden, which was endowed with splendor on all sides and resembled the Vaibhrāja forest, the Lord of the World spoke to the Goddess.
O auspicious Goddess, in this place where I formerly dwelt,
foam from the force of the milk being drunk by the self-born calves of the cows situated above in Goloka fell upon my head. || 9 ||
Then I saw those cows above me, on the side of Soma.
Then, as they were looked upon by me there, those cows became scorched by my splendor; afflicted intensely, they assumed many different colors. || 11 ||
"O Goddess, these cows were formerly born of a uniform tawny color; they did not possess various colors when they were first beheld by me. || 12 ||
O Daughter of the Mountain, having recognized their capacity to provide refuge, Soma approached them and, coming from all sides with those flowing streams, took shelter in me alone.
Then, by the cows who were thus afflicted, Brahmā spoke to me: "O Lord of Gods, O you who are worshipped by all the deities, show favor so that these cows, through your splendor,
may not perish this very instant."
Then, O Goddess, I myself established myself in this very place;
I am renowned as Goprekṣa, praised by all the deities.
A human being who comes to Goprekṣeśvara, beholds me, and worships me— || 16 ||
One does not fall into an evil rebirth and is liberated from all taints; then, while I was pleased, those cows, being scorched, approached this lake and shone forth there, tranquilized. ||17||
From that time forward, it has been called Kapilāhrada.
"In this place as well, O Goddess, I myself, known by the name Vṛṣadhvaja, have established my presence; behold him standing here. || 19 ||
Having bathed at this sacred ford of the Kapilā lake with a focused mind and having beheld this bull-bannered Lord, a man shall obtain the fruit of all sacrifices. 8.29.20
Moreover, having worshipped me here, even after death one attains residence in the same world;
and upon the dissolution of the body, one obtains the status of a Gaṇa, which is exceedingly difficult to attain.
In this very place, moreover, all those cows were themselves milked by Brahmā for the sake of the peace of all the worlds; their milk was nectar.
From that milk, this enchanting lake was produced.
The auspicious and meritorious Devahrada, renowned as Bhadradoha, [is located there]. ||23||
"O Goddess, I have been propitiated in this place by all the gods:
'Go, O Lord, to a state of peace. Thereupon, having become Śiva-Upaśānta (the Quiescent Śiva), I remained established here; even the sight of me is meritorious."
Upon seeing him, a mortal who is self-restrained shall attain the heavenly world. || 25 ||
"Here I was brought and established by Brahmā, the Supreme Lord;
and having taken me from Brahmā, I was established here again by Viṣṇu.
Then Viṣṇu was addressed by Brahmā with an agitated mind:
"This linga was brought by me; for what reason have you installed it? ||37||
Viṣṇu spoke again to Brahmā, whose face was filled with anger:
"My supreme devotion toward the god Rudra is exceedingly great. (28)
"By me this has been established; therefore, it shall belong to you by that name—namely, Hiraṇyagarbha. Thus have I remained here.
Even upon seeing him, O Lord of Gods, a man shall go to my world."

Then once again, O auspicious one, Brahmā installed this *liṅga* of mine according to the prescribed rites, endowed with supreme devotion. I myself am established here as Svalīneśvara. || 8.29.30-31 ||
Dissolved within myself, who am beyond the other [the individual soul], in Pradhāna, my causal source;
therefore, this secret field of mine is remembered as "Svalīna" (dissolved-in-itself). ||32||
Having abandoned his vital breaths here, a man is never born again anywhere;
that is his infinite goal, and it is remembered as such for yogins as well.
Even in this very region, there was a Daitya who was a thorn in the side of the gods.
Having assumed the form of a tiger, the proud and powerful one was slain. ||34||
Therefore, he became renowned as Vyāghreśvara; I am always established here, so that upon seeing this Maheśvara, one shall not fall into a miserable state again.

O auspicious one, those two Daityas, Utpala and Vidala, who were created by Brahmā in the past as arrogant beings to be slain by women, have been killed by you here with a contemptuous kick of the ball;
this is the mark he has left behind.
"In the beginning, I came here and remained together with the lords of the Gaṇas.
Therefore, this is my preeminent station, and its sight is meritorious.
Having seen this Liṅga of mine, which is established in that preeminent station," ||37-38||
The mortal who has attained perfection no longer grieves over death and birth;
indeed, all the deities have established their emblems on every side. 39.
Upon seeing this, a mortal will certainly become a member of my retinue after the dissolution of the body;
for I myself have come here and remained present. And because I have not departed from this place, it is therefore called Avimukta (the Unreleased).
The sacred field of Vārāṇasī shall become a bestower of liberation. ||41||
Indeed, whatever man shall behold me here as Avimukteśvara,
his destination shall be that of the Gaṇas, wherever he may die.
Having here renounced your vital breaths, you shall attain the highest liberation, just as it was done formerly by your father, Himavat, the king of mountains himself. (43)
Knowing that this place is dear to me, a linga has been installed;
behold this which stands here, renowned as Śaileśvara. (44)
O Goddess, having seen this, a person shall not follow the path of an evil rebirth;
for this river Vārāṇasī is meritorious and a liberator from sin. 45.
Having adorned this sacred field, the Ganges joined it;
and at this confluence, Brahmā established an excellent liṅga.
Let it be seen that it is renowned in the world as Saṅgameśvara;
for whatever pure man bathes at the confluence of the two divine rivers [47].
One should worship Saṅgameśāna; whence could there be fear of rebirth for him?
This other great sacred field is the supreme abode of yogins. (48)
And in the midst of that field, where I myself have become established, it is renowned by all the gods and asuras as "Madhyameśvara. (49)
For this is indeed the abode of the perfected ones who practice my vows—of yogins seeking liberation, whose selves have conquered birth and death. (8.29.50)
Having seen this Madhyameśāna, one does not grieve regarding rebirth;
and this Liṅga has been installed by Śukra, your son. (51)
Known by the name Śukreśvara, it is worshipped by all the Siddhas and immortals;
upon seeing this, a human being shall immediately be liberated from all sins. (52)
And once dead, that man shall not undergo rebirth in saṃsāra again.
Formerly, in the form of jackals, the Asuras were thorns to the gods. (53)
Having obtained a boon from Brahmā, they were struck down by me, O Daughter of Himavat, while I was in the form of Jambuka, fearing the killing of a jackal. Thus indeed am I. (54)
I was renowned throughout the world and honored by gods and asuras;
even by seeing this Lord of Gods, one shall obtain all desires. ||55||
Indeed, these were established by the planets, with Venus at their head.
"Behold my meritorious lingas, which grant all desires!
Thus, O Pārvatī, these meritorious places of my residence within the sacred field have been described to you; now hear this other secret."
This field is proclaimed to extend for one *krośa* in each of the four directions;
... O lady of lovely limbs, it bestows immortality at the time of death. (58)
...established in Sthāna and Kedāra;
having seen this field, the state of being a Gaṇa is attained and liberation is reached. ||59||
Since from that station of Gaṇapati there arises supreme liberation,
it is therefore superior even to Mahālaya and to Kedāra as well as Madhyama.
O auspicious one, this Avimukta is remembered as the most meritorious field;
it is located in the middle of Kedāra and is indeed the Mahālaya site.
Among my merits in the world of mortals, this is indeed the most excellent:
that when the worlds were purified, this auspicious field [arose] from that.
Because it was never released by me, it became known as Avimukta. Having beheld the Liṅga of Avimukteśvara here, a human being [attains liberation]. || 63 ||
Immediately liberated from sin, one is released from the bonds of *paśu*;
[one should visit] Śaileśa, Saṅgameśa, Svalīna, and Madhyameśvara. ||64||
Hiraṇyagarbha, Īśāna, Goprekṣa, he who has the bull as his banner, Upaśāntaśiva, and likewise the one dwelling in Jyeṣṭhasthāna. || 65 ||
Having beheld the renowned Śukreśvara, Vyāghreśa, and Jambukeśvara,
a mortal is not born again in this ocean of worldly suffering.
Sanatkumāra said:
Having spoken thus, Mahādeva gazed toward all the directions.
After beholding Maheśvara, the God of gods, as he remained [there], [she stood] behind him.
Suddenly that entire field became as if ablaze,
with the sound of thunder and lightning, like ten million suns risen at once.
Filled on one side with splendors like those of fire and the sun,
there appeared the Siddhas of the Pāśupata sect, white-hued from their smearing of ashes.
Many lords of yogis, great-souled ones who observe the sacrificial vows,
and those whose emblems were unmanifest, blazing with the splendor of Śiva-yoga,
suddenly approached and paid homage to Maheśvara.
Having gazed again upon the Lord of Gods and having performed the entirety of meditative yoga,
they stood with their souls fixed [on Him], as if dissolving into the Lord.
As they remained thus, the God of gods, the Lord of Umā, [addressed them].
Having intentionally assumed a supreme form, the Lord became a Person;
he is the twenty-sixth principle, the unmanifest Ishvara, possessing a splendor equal to ten thousand suns.
As the Lord of the World assumed that supreme form, standing as if intoxicated to bring the entire universe together within himself,
the Daughter of the Mountain King was unable to behold his body, her hair standing on end with awe.
Then, perceiving herself to be joyful and established in her true nature, she— ||75||
Having assumed through yoga a form composed of the supreme self, he was unable to behold the body of the Puruṣa, the Supreme Soul. ||76||
Then, having attained dissolution within the Supreme Person, all those yogis— whose seeds of worldly existence had been burnt— entered his heart.
Thereafter, he bestowed grace upon all those perfected ones, the foremost among ascetics.
Then, abiding in his blue-and-red form, he again assumed an auspicious body.
Seeing that, the Daughter of the Mountain, her every hair standing on end with joy, went before him and, praising him, asked: "O Blessed One, who are these? (78–79)
Then the best of the gods spoke to that goddess, the daughter of the mountain king:
"By those excellent twice-born ones who, having undertaken my vow, have practiced yoga here with devotion,
[liberation] shall be attained in a single birth."

"By the power of this field, by my devotion, and through my contemplation, I indeed bestow such grace that always grants liberation. Therefore, this great field of mine is served by Brahmā and the other gods. (81–82)
O Goddess, in my abode at Vārāṇasī, on the eighth and fourteenth days of every month, both fortnights, the best of Brahmins who are learned in the Vedas and perfected ascetics [should worship]. (83)
And during an eclipse of the moon or the sun, and especially on the full-moon day of the month of Kārttika.
On all auspicious festival days, at the equinoxes and solstices, all the sacred fords on earth are present in Vārāṇasī, yet the Jāhnavī [is preeminent] there. (85)
Flowing northward, this meritorious and auspicious stream has issued from my crest;
it flows down from your father, the Himavat, the king of mountains.
They resort to it from all sides; listen to them, O fair-faced one:
Sannihitī along with Kurukṣetra and hundreds of other sacred fords.
Puṣkara, Naimiṣa, Prayāga, and Pṛthūdaka;
